title: GitHub - verfy-dev/verfy: Verfy CLI (MIT): lock MCP tool definitions and block tools that change after you approved them, guard every Claude Code tool call, signed receipts. pip install verfy
excerpt: Verfy CLI (MIT): lock MCP tool definitions and block tools that change after you approved them, guard every Claude Code tool call, signed receipts. pip install verfy - verfy-dev/verfy
content_html:
The server changes the tool's description after you approved it. Verfy notices the new SHA-256 and blocks the call. Try it on the website.

python fix.py looks harmless as a command. Verfy reads the script before it runs and names the line that would wipe the home folder.

▶ The 60-second version (MP4, 1.1 MB): pin the tools, the server ships an update, verfy lock check fails, the gateway hides the tool and denies the call. Recorded with verfy 0.17.0: every terminal line is real output of its demo server (python -m verfy.demo_server --rugpull).

Stop what your agent shouldn't do. Prove what it did. For Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, GitHub Copilot and Devin: Verfy checks each tool call before it runs, stops a tool that changes in secret, and signs a receipt for every call it checks.

Where to go: bugs and questions in issues; security reports privately, as SECURITY.md describes.

The Verfy CLI is MIT and always will be. Verfy Cloud is a paid hosted service (free for now; paid plans are not on sale yet). This repository is the CLI; the hosted service is developed separately.

Verfy checks every tool call a coding agent makes against your policy before it runs, locks the MCP tool definitions the agent may use, and writes an Ed25519-signed, hash-chained receipt for every call it checks. Verfy Cloud, the hosted service, gives an organization one policy, tool-change approvals, device management, an audit log and evidence exports that anyone can verify offline.

Part What it does
Verfy Lock verfy.lock pins the SHA-256 of every tool definition, and of the files an agent loads (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills, hook settings); a changed tool is hidden and denied until someone reviews the diff, and verfy lock check (or the GitHub Action in action.yml) fails CI. Each change is explained in words with a risk level.
Verfy Receipts verfy.receipt/1: signed, chained, hash-only by default; verfy verify detects edits, deletions and reordering; verfy scitt export writes SCITT signed statements (COSE_Sign1).
Verfy Guard Deterministic allow / ask / deny for shell commands, file paths, URLs, SQL, payments and leaked secrets, through a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, hooks for Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Devin, or an MCP gateway. Errors never become allow.
Verfy Scan Finds MCP servers in Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, VS Code and Windsurf configs; flags tool poisoning, hidden instructions, shadowing, invisible Unicode, unpinned packages, plain-http servers and secrets in configs. verfy import reads Snyk Agent Scan and Cisco MCP Scanner findings so the gateway can enforce them.
Verfy Sandbox verfy run --sandbox starts a command, an MCP server or the agent inside Anthropic's open source sandbox runtime, with settings from your policy: no network except the hosts you allow, writes only in this folder, no reading credentials. macOS, Linux, and Windows through WSL2. verfy sandbox status and sync check Claude Code's own sandbox.
Verfy Cloud Hosted by Verfy: one team policy, device enrollment, server-verified receipts, lock and call approvals, Slack and Telegram alerts, audit log, evidence exports. Devices connect with one command, verfy init --url … --code …, and then upload receipts on their own.

Verfy and scanners

Scanners judge a tool when you scan it. Verfy is built for what happens after: the tool changes, the agent calls it, and someone later asks what ran. Use both. From each project's own README, checked 2026-11-05 at the versions listed on the page (full table and sources):

Snyk Agent Scan (formerly Invariant mcp-scan) Cisco MCP Scanner mcp-context-protector (Trail of Bits) Verfy
How tools are judged Local checks + Snyk API YARA locally; optional LLM / AI Defense API Pinning; optional guardrail model Deterministic local rules
Account needed Snyk account No (YARA) No No
Notices a tool changed after approval Not described Not described Yes (trust-on-first-use pinning) Yes (verfy.lock)
Fails the pull request when a tool changed Not described Not described Not described Yes (GitHub Action)
Checks calls as they happen Agent Guard hooks, answers from the Snyk API No Blocks unapproved servers; response guardrails Claude Code hook (all tools) + MCP gateway
Signed record of each call Not described No Not described Ed25519, hash-chained, SCITT export

They also do things Verfy does not: Snyk scans agent skills, Cisco reads server source code and scans packages and binaries, and context-protector can run a guardrail model over tool responses.

Quick start: the CLI

pip install verfy                # Python ≥ 3.10, no dependencies (no Python? see "Without Python" below)
verfy init                       # signing key + starter policy in ~/.verfy, the MCP servers found, the Claude Code hook if you want it
verfy scan --discover            # check the MCP servers your agents can reach
verfy lock check --update        # lock the tools in .mcp.json into ./verfy.lock (commit it)
verfy hook install --write       # guard every Claude Code tool call (or install the plugin, below)
verfy lock files --update        # lock CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills and hook settings too
verfy check "rm -rf ~"           # exit 2: deny (VFY-SH-001)
verfy demo                       # a poisoned MCP server behind the gateway
verfy verify                     # every signature and link in your ledger

Without Python, an install script downloads a standalone build. Download it, read it, then run it (there is no curl … | sh one-liner on purpose: Verfy itself asks about that pattern, rule VFY-SH-005):

curl -fsSLO https://verfy.dev/install.sh && less install.sh && sh install.sh      # macOS, Linux
powershell -c "irm https://verfy.dev/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1"           # Windows: download,
notepad install.ps1                                                                           # read,
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1                                         # run

As a Claude Code plugin

claude plugin marketplace add verfy-dev/verfy-releases
claude plugin install verfy@verfy

The plugin installs the same hook for every session, plus a skill that lets Claude check your locks for you (approving changes stays with you). It calls the verfy command, so install the CLI first. Details: plugins/verfy/README.md.

More: verfy-cli/README.md and the docs at https://verfy.dev/docs.

Repository layout

verfy-cli/           the Python CLI (guard, scan, lock, receipts, hook, gateway, team client) and its tests
verfy-cli/js/        the JavaScript twin of the rule engine, checked against the same fixtures
action.yml           the GitHub Action that runs `verfy lock check` in CI
plugins/verfy/       the Claude Code plugin (hook + skill); .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lists it
advisories/          Verfy Advisories: public, sourced vulnerabilities in MCP servers and agent tools (OSV), added by pull request
install/             the one-line installers served at verfy.dev/install.sh and /install.ps1
research/            how often MCP tool definitions change between releases (method, code, workflow)
docs/                limitations, research write-ups, assets

Tests

cd verfy-cli && python -m unittest discover -s tests     # Python tests, incl. cross-engine checks (needs Node)
node verfy-cli/tests/test_engine.mjs                     # the JavaScript engine against the shared fixtures

Limits

Verfy's checks are not a sandbox: its rules are deterministic pattern matching, and it only sees calls that pass through its hook or gateway. For untrusted code, use verfy run --sandbox, a container or a VM. A receipt proves what Verfy decided and that the record was not changed afterwards, not what a tool did internally. No independent penetration test has been done yet. Full list: docs/SECURITY_LIMITATIONS.md.

Contributing, security, trademarks

  • Contributions are welcome: see CONTRIBUTING.md. You sign the CLA once, by commenting on your first pull request.
  • Found a way past Verfy? That is a vulnerability: report it privately as described in SECURITY.md.
  • "Verfy" and the logo are trademarks: forks need another name. See TRADEMARKS.md.

License

The code in this repository is MIT licensed (see LICENSE), and the CLI will stay MIT. Earlier versions of this repository also contained the web platform that is now Verfy Cloud; those versions remain available under MIT in the history. New work on the hosted service is not open source.

Verfy Guard Deterministic allow / ask / deny for shell commands, file paths, URLs, SQL, payments and leaked secrets, through a Claude Code PreToolUse hook, hooks for Cursor, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and Devin, or an MCP gateway. Errors never become allow.
Verfy Scan Finds MCP servers in Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, VS Code and Windsurf configs; flags tool poisoning, hidden instructions, shadowing, invisible Unicode, unpinned packages, plain-http servers and secrets in configs. verfy import reads Snyk Agent Scan and Cisco MCP Scanner findings so the gateway can enforce them.
Verfy Sandbox verfy run --sandbox starts a command, an MCP server or the agent inside Anthropic's open source sandbox runtime, with settings from your policy: no network except the hosts you allow, writes only in this folder, no reading credentials. macOS, Linux, and Windows through WSL2. verfy sandbox status and sync check Claude Code's own sandbox.
Verfy Cloud Hosted by Verfy: one team policy, device enrollment, server-verified receipts, lock and call approvals, Slack and Telegram alerts, audit log, evidence exports. Devices connect with one command, verfy init --url … --code …, and then upload receipts on their own.

Verfy and scanners

Scanners judge a tool when you scan it. Verfy is built for what happens after: the tool changes, the agent calls it, and someone later asks what ran. Use both. From each project's own README, checked 2026-11-05 at the versions listed on the page (full table and sources):

Snyk Agent Scan (formerly Invariant mcp-scan) Cisco MCP Scanner mcp-context-protector (Trail of Bits) Verfy
How tools are judged Local checks + Snyk API YARA locally; optional LLM / AI Defense API Pinning; optional guardrail model Deterministic local rules
Account needed Snyk account No (YARA) No No
Notices a tool changed after approval Not described Not described Yes (trust-on-first-use pinning) Yes (verfy.lock)
Fails the pull request when a tool changed Not described Not described Not described Yes (GitHub Action)
Checks calls as they happen Agent Guard hooks, answers from the Snyk API No Blocks unapproved servers; response guardrails Claude Code hook (all tools) + MCP gateway
Signed record of each call Not described No Not described Ed25519, hash-chained, SCITT export

They also do things Verfy does not: Snyk scans agent skills, Cisco reads server source code and scans packages and binaries, and context-protector can run a guardrail model over tool responses.

Quick start: the CLI

pip install verfy                # Python ≥ 3.10, no dependencies (no Python? see "Without Python" below)
verfy init                       # signing key + starter policy in ~/.verfy, the MCP servers found, the Claude Code hook if you want it
verfy scan --discover            # check the MCP servers your agents can reach
verfy lock check --update        # lock the tools in .mcp.json into ./verfy.lock (commit it)
verfy hook install --write       # guard every Claude Code tool call (or install the plugin, below)
verfy lock files --update        # lock CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules, skills and hook settings too
verfy check "rm -rf ~"           # exit 2: deny (VFY-SH-001)
verfy demo                       # a poisoned MCP server behind the gateway
verfy verify                     # every signature and link in your ledger

Without Python, an install script downloads a standalone build. Download it, read it, then run it (there is no curl … | sh one-liner on purpose: Verfy itself asks about that pattern, rule VFY-SH-005):

curl -fsSLO https://verfy.dev/install.sh && less install.sh && sh install.sh      # macOS, Linux
powershell -c "irm https://verfy.dev/install.ps1 -OutFile install.ps1"           # Windows: download,
notepad install.ps1                                                                           # read,
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1                                         # run

As a Claude Code plugin

claude plugin marketplace add verfy-dev/verfy-releases
claude plugin install verfy@verfy

The plugin installs the same hook for every session, plus a skill that lets Claude check your locks for you (approving changes stays with you). It calls the verfy command, so install the CLI first. Details: plugins/verfy/README.md.

More: verfy-cli/README.md and the docs at https://verfy.dev/docs.

存储库布局

verfy-cli/           the Python CLI (guard, scan, lock, receipts, hook, gateway, team client) and its tests
verfy-cli/js/        the JavaScript twin of the rule engine, checked against the same fixtures
action.yml           the GitHub Action that runs `verfy lock check` in CI
plugins/verfy/       the Claude Code plugin (hook + skill); .claude-plugin/marketplace.json lists it
advisories/          Verfy Advisories: public, sourced vulnerabilities in MCP servers and agent tools (OSV), added by pull request
install/             the one-line installers served at verfy.dev/install.sh and /install.ps1
research/            how often MCP tool definitions change between releases (method, code, workflow)
docs/                limitations, research write-ups, assets

Tests

cd verfy-cli && python -m unittest discover -s tests     # Python tests, incl. cross-engine checks (needs Node)
node verfy-cli/tests/test_engine.mjs                     # the JavaScript engine against the shared fixtures

限制

Verfy's checks are not a sandbox: its rules are deterministic pattern matching, and it only sees calls that pass through its hook or gateway. For untrusted code, use verfy run --sandbox, a container or a VM. A receipt proves what Verfy decided and that the record was not changed afterwards, not what a tool did internally. No independent penetration test has been done yet. Full list: docs/SECURITY_LIMITATIONS.md.
